AN ACT to amend the election law, in relation to signatures for designating

items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4002

SPONSOR: MAY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the election law, in relation to signatures for desig-
nating petitions for political subdivisions outside the city of New
York; and providing for the repeal of such provisions upon expiration
thereof

 
PURPOSE OF BILL:

To ensure ballot access for a variety of candidates for office due to
the recent change in the primary election date.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section one of this bill adds a new subdivision 5 of § 6-136 of the
election law to reduce the minimum petition signature requirement for
all public offices to be filled in 2019, with the exception of offices
in New York City, to 3.75 percent of the enrolled voters of the party
residing within the political unit in which the office or position is to
be voted for.

Section two is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In 2019, after 8 years of impasse the legislature has passed legislation
reunifying state, local and federal (non-presidential) primary elections
to be held on the 4th Tuesday in June, effective immediately.

However, because of the imminent change in the political calendar neces-
sary to meet the requirements for a June primary, candidates for local
offices in 2019 are required to begin circulating designating petitions
at the end of February 2019, rather than in mid-June, 2019.  This bill
would temporarily reduce the number of signatures required for designat-
ing petitions by 1/4 for candidates running for office, with the excep-
tion of NYC, in 2019 to allow candidates to organize their campaigns,
print their petitions, and begin collecting voters' signatures after the
change in the primary date.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately and shall expire December 31,
2019 when upon such date the provisions of this act shall be deemed
repealed.

summary: Relates to signatures for designating petitions for political subdivisions outside the city of New York; must be signed by not less than three and three-quarters per centum.
